If the impact of the AFES upon use of cast iron and steel is assessed from the view point that all fuel economy measures likely to be taken to improve fuel economy from MY 1976 levels to the level established by the AFES, are attributable to the AFES, then the impact of the AFES upon cast iron and steel is likely to be a reduction in consumption of cast iron and steel by 42 million pounds. This reduction is the result of reductions in average engine size (CID) and average vehicle weight. The magnitude of the reduction was calculated as follows:
• · · · · · · · · · · · · · · · · · · ·
The Agency derived a relationship between percent reduction in CID, and percent reduction in vehicle weight. This was done by comparing the average weight and average CID of a vehicle fleet representative of the industry before the shift to smaller engines, with the average weight and average CID of the fleet after the shift to smaller engines. As a result of this comparison, the agency estimates that the percent weight reduction in cast iron and steel is equal to 0.109 multiplied by the percent CID reduction. If this relationship is applied to the amount of CID reduction which is likely to result to achieve compliance with the proposed AFES, the savings in cast iron and steel is approximately 18.2 million pounds.
